salient_findings: 1-year history of slow but progressive swelling near the gluteal cleft
4 × 4 cm area of swelling with mild blanching erythema
No fluid obtained on percutaneous aspiration
Complex and septated 6 × 4 × 4 cm mass excised from subcutaneous tissue
key_facts: 32-year-old woman
1-year history of swelling
Swelling located near the gluteal cleft
No fevers, chills, pain, drainage, bleeding, or rectal bleeding
Mild blanching erythema of the overlying skin
No fluctuance, purulence, or visible pilonidal pits
Percutaneous aspiration yielded no fluid
Complex and septated mass excised from subcutaneous tissue
Mass was adherent to subcutaneous fat but did not involve the coccyx or anal sphincter

shortlist.label: Epidermoid cyst
shortlist.why_kept: matches the description of a complex and septated mass in the subcutaneous tissue

shortlist.label: Dermoid cyst
shortlist.why_kept: consistent with the presence of a swelling and erythema near the gluteal cleft

shortlist.label: Pilomatricoma
shortlist.why_kept: possible cause of a slow-growing mass in the subcutaneous tissue

shortlist.label: Lipoma
shortlist.why_kept: adherent to subcutaneous fat, which is consistent with the clinical findings

shortlist.label: Desmoid tumor
shortlist.why_kept: can present as a slow-growing mass in the subcutaneous tissue, although less common

raw.rationale: The complex and septated mass excised from the subcutaneous tissue, along with the location near the gluteal cleft and absence of symptoms like fevers or drainage, is most consistent with an epidermoid cyst, which is a type of inclusion cyst.

rejected.label: Dermoid cyst
rejected.why: While similar to epidermoid cysts, dermoid cysts typically contain skin appendages and are less likely given the description.

rejected.label: Pilomatricoma
rejected.why: Pilomatricomas are usually found on the head or neck and are less common in the gluteal area.

rejected.label: Lipoma
rejected.why: Lipomas are benign tumors of fat tissue but do not typically present as complex and septated masses.

rejected.label: Desmoid tumor
rejected.why: Desmoid tumors are aggressive and can cause significant symptoms, which does not match the patient's 1-year history of slow but progressive swelling without significant symptoms.
